ticket.title: scope consumers to the dependents of changed crates: 11 min for a full pass cannot sit in a commit chain
ticket.description: `outfeed consumers` compiles all 11 members every time, measured at 11.0 min warm on darwin/stable/sequential (OF-43). That is affordable as an on-demand check and not affordable inside a per-commit chain, which is why OF-43 did not wire it in. The useful scope is tiny by comparison: when a change touches a shared crate, only that crate dependents can break, and SP-41 demonstrated it - three consumers in three repositories, dozens of crates untouched. Wanted: derive the dependent set from cargo metadata (the workspace already resolves the whole graph), build only those, and fall back to a full pass when the changed set cannot be determined - including when a lockfile or the patch table changed, since either can move every edge. Acceptance: a contract edit in common builds and checks only the crates that depend on gaugeblock-contracts and finishes in well under a minute on the same warm tree that took 11.0 min for a full pass; a change touching no shared crate checks nothing and says so rather than reporting a vacuous pass.
